#+TITLE: 01 code.reading -- learn rea's architecture by writing its postmortem, then map rea into prg
#+STARTUP: overview

* Dev process setup
  Before executing ANY work item in this plan, open and obey the rules in
  this repo's instructions:

    - AGENTS.md            (rea's rules: inward deps, Evidence provenance,
                            tagged errors, owned processes, tokens > time > cpu)
    - CONTRIBUTING.md

  And, because this checkout is a fleet repo, the cluster contract:

    - /workspace/cluster/.github/copilot-instructions.md  (R-MEASURE, R-ROOM,
      R-BENCHPLACE, R-MASTER-ONLY, git discipline)

  This plan does not restate either.  Where they conflict for files under
  .github/REPL/ (rea: "never commit local planning artifacts"; cluster:
  "commit per work item"), this plan's ruling: .github/REPL/ lives ONLY on
  our fork's master (origin = github.com/bartuer/rea), never in a PR to
  upstream (morluto/rea).

  :ADDED_2026-10-18 (user: "/prg on commit history and skills folder, have a
  postmortem copy in repo and /org_plan create 01.code.reading.org.txt by learn
  architecture via postmortem writing ... we will have the capability to read

  This plan runs on a multi-machine environment described in:

    - ${FLEET_HOME:-$HOME/.fleet}/cluster.md

  Read it before executing.  Where it defines parallelism, it outranks
  subagent fan-out.  This plan does not restate it.

* Goal [0/4]
  - [ ] G1 rea builds and runs on an odsp box; `rea capabilities --json` lists which tools are
        available WITHOUT any bring-your-own engine.  (Phase A)
  - [ ] G2 .github/REPL/postmortem.md exists, written per .github/REPL/postmortem, cites commits,
        and a reader can draw rea's layer diagram from its first section alone.  (Phase B)
  - [ ] G3 .github/REPL/fix.archive/rea-prg-integration.md: how rea output enters prg
        (folder -> bin2md --corpus -> case.prg.db), with :decision:/:rejected: per choice.  (Phase C)
  - [ ] G4 one binary on c05 answered end to end: `rea ... --json` -> folder -> prg ask,
        and /workspace/cluster/.github/skills/rea/SKILL.md points at the result.  (Phase Z)

* Frontier (consequential choices, decided up front)
  - :decision: read rea, do not fork its code.  Our fork carries ONLY .github/REPL/; master
    tracks upstream main by merge.  :rejected: patching rea now -- we do not yet know what to patch.
  - :decision: integrate through the CLI + files (rea --json > DIR), the purl shape: a producer
    that lands files prg already reads.  :rejected: rea MCP inside prg -- prg is shell + rg + jq;
    an MCP client is a new runtime for the same JSON.  Revisit only if Phase C measures a
    multi-call workflow that one CLI call cannot express.
  - :decision: no engine installs in this plan (Ghidra/IDA/JADX are BYO).  Phase A measures what
    works with objdump + node alone.  :rejected: installing Ghidra on 34 boxes before we know a
    question that needs it (R-ALLBOX cost).
  - :open: node 24.14 vs rea's sqlite 24.15 floor -- a fleet node bump is a separate R-ALLBOX
    plan; Phase A records the gap, does not fix it.

* KISS audit (of this plan)
  - 4 phases, no code beyond one SKILL.md and one spike script.  No new service, no new room
    protocol, no new DB.  The postmortem is the architecture reading -- no separate notes doc.
  - Cut: a per-provider tour (29 dirs).  Phase B reads the layers, not every provider.

* Main Loop
  - (R) run the phase :test_tool:, read which line failed
  - (E) fix the doc/script, not the test
  - (P) re-run :test_tool:
  - (L) until it passes; then `done --ref <sha>` with the test output

* TODO Phase A -- build and smoke rea on odsp [0/3]
  :needs: {"tier":"wsl","island":"odsp","box":"c05"}
  - [ ] A.1 `npm ci && npm run build:cached` in /workspace/rea (npm 11.9 vs pinned 11.16: try as is;
        record the error if any, use `npx -y npm@11.16.0 ci` only if needed).
  - [ ] A.2 `node scripts/rea.mjs capabilities --json > /tmp/rea01/cap.json`; tabulate
        available vs unavailable + availability_code.
  - [ ] A.3 smoke three engine-free reads, each saved as JSON:
        (a) native artifact on /usr/local/bin/bin2md (objdump provider or inspect-artifact),
        (b) a JavaScript tree (rea's own dist/ or a node_modules package) via analyze-javascript-application,
        (c) inspect-sqlite-database on a case.prg.db (expect unsupported_version on node 24.14 -- record it).
  - :test_tool: `jq -r '.. | objects | select(has("available")) | [.name,.available] | @tsv' /tmp/rea01/cap.json | head` prints rows,
                and `ls /tmp/rea01/*.json | wc -l` >= 3.

* TODO Phase B -- architecture reading = write the postmortem [0/3]
  :needs: {"tier":"wsl","island":"odsp","box":"c05"}
  - [ ] B.1 /prg over: git log (index in /tmp/rea-idx), docs/architecture.mermaid, AGENTS.md,
        docs/tool-design.md, docs/testing.md, docs/roadmap.md, .agents/skills/**.
  - [ ] B.2 write .github/REPL/postmortem.md per .github/REPL/postmortem: section 1 = the layer map
        (entry -> composition -> application -> providers -> process -> contracts -> domain) and the one
        dominant lesson; then findings, one paragraph each, each citing >= 1 commit sha.
        Candidate lessons to verify, not assume: owned-process lifecycle (263 hits), Evidence
        observation/derivation/inference/unknown split, Python MCP -> Node rewrite, "no fallback"
        provider selection, removal pressure (102 removes, 66 breaking).
  - [ ] B.3 frontier/kiss section: gains, losses, what got built that need not have, open questions.
  - :test_tool: `f=.github/REPL/postmortem.md; wc -l $f; rg -c '\b[0-9a-f]{9}\b' $f; for s in $(rg -o '\b[0-9a-f]{9}\b' $f | sort -u); do git cat-file -e $s || echo BAD $s; done`
                -> >= 300 lines, >= 20 sha cites, no BAD.
